title: Support and annihilation by an ideal power on a Noetherian algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Noetherian means locally Noetherian on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-locnoeth], quasi-compact, and quasi-separated; the last two conditions mean that every open cover has a finite subcover and the diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Modules are on the small etale ringed site, with quasi-coherence as in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. On a locally Noetherian space, coherent means quasi-coherent with coherent pullbacks on all etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $\operatorname{Supp}(M)$ for the locus of nonzero geometric stalks, with the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. A closed immersion is representable and a closed immersion after every scheme base change [def-weil-closed-immersion]; reduced means that etale scheme charts have local rings without nonzero nilpotents, and irreducible means nonempty and not the union of two proper closed subsets. Assume $X$ is Noetherian. Let $F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed subspace. Put $I=\ker(\mathcal O_X\to i_*\mathcal O_Z)$, its quasi-coherent defining ideal. Direct image is [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Define $I^0F=F$ and $I^{n+1}F=I(I^nF)$, where $IM$ is the submodule generated locally by products of sections of $I$ and $M$. For every $n\geq0$, $I^nF$ and $F/I^nF$ are coherent. One has $$\operatorname{Supp}(F)\subseteq |i|(|Z|)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists n\geq0,\ I^nF=0.$$ No reducedness of $Z$ is assumed.

proof.text: On an etale scheme chart $e:T\to X$, pullback is restriction [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Write $J=I|_T$ and let $G$ be the quasi-coherent Zariski module corresponding to $F|_T$ under [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence]. The ideal correspondence [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence] makes $J$ the quasi-coherent ideal of $Z\times_XT$. Restriction commutes with the locally generated products in the statement: a local finite sum $\sum a_jm_j$ restricts to the identical sum, and every such sum on a chart object is already a sum on that object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. Induction gives $(I^nF)|_T=(J^nG)_{\mathrm{et}}$, starting with $n=0$. For quotients, local representatives modulo these submodules give the same comparison. Indeed the scheme product and quotient are quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections], inductively on $n$; the exact associated-sheaf functor [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-module-exact-finiteness-comparison] identifies their inclusions and cokernels with the small-etale ones. Its section formula and the equivalence's identity on open sections identify the multiplication on both sides. Thus $I^nF$ and $F/I^nF$ are quasi-coherent: the local presentations of these chart modules are presentations on the slice sites, exactly the local condition in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module].

source.place: Tag 07UD, lemma-coherent-Noetherian-quasi-coherent-sub-quotient, and the chart restriction used in Tag 07UK; scheme products: Tags 01I8/01IC; exact small-etale association: Tag 06VE(5).

proof.text: For every $n$, Step 1 supplies the quasi-coherent submodule $I^nF\subseteq F$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-noetherian-coherent-support] to this submodule of the coherent module $F$ on the locally Noetherian space $X$. It states precisely that both the submodule and its quotient are coherent. This proves both coherence assertions, including $n=0$, where the submodule is $F$ and the quotient is zero.

Quasi-compactness gives an affine surjective etale atlas $p:U\to X$ by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. The scheme $U$ is locally Noetherian because it is an etale chart of $X$ (the hypothesis explicitly includes every such chart). It is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], hence Noetherian in the scheme sense. Set $G=F|_U$, viewed as a coherent Zariski module as in Step 1 and the definition of coherence in the item. Let $J=I|_U$ and $Z_U=Z\times_XU$. By [lem-sfb-space-ideal-closed-subspace-correspondence], $J$ is the defining ideal of $Z_U$. Thus $V(J)=|p|^{-1}(|i|(|Z|))$: a point $u$ belongs to either side exactly when its field-valued map into $X$ factors through the closed subspace after a field extension, equivalently when the defining ideal maps to zero in the residue field. This is the affine closed-immersion description in [def-weil-closed-immersion].

source.place: Tag 07UK, proof, choice of an affine surjective etale atlas and its Noetherianity; Tag 03MB, lemma-closed-immersion-ideals.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-space-etale-chart-support], $\operatorname{Supp}_U(G)=|p|^{-1}(\operatorname{Supp}_X(F))$. Since $|p|$ is surjective, taking inverse images detects the inclusion of these two subsets. Together with Step 3 this gives $\operatorname{Supp}_X(F)\subseteq|i|(|Z|)$ if and only if $\operatorname{Supp}_U(G)\subseteq V(J)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-support-power-ideal-kills] to the Noetherian scheme $U$, its coherent module $G$, and its quasi-coherent ideal $J$. The latter condition holds if and only if $J^tG=0$ for some $t\geq0$, where that node's $J^tG$ is the product of the ideal power $J^t$ with $G$. This is the iterated module $J^nG=J(J^{n-1}G)$ of Step 1 for $t=n$: by [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1) all intermediate modules are quasi-coherent, and by its clause (2), by induction on $n$, both have sections $J(V)^nG(V)$ on every affine open $V\subseteq U$. Quasi-coherent submodules of $G$ with the same sections on all affine opens are equal; for $n=0$ both are $G$. In particular this supplies one exponent on the whole affine atlas, rather than exponents on infinitely many charts.

source.place: Tag 07UK, proof, reduction of support to the atlas and application of coherent.tex Tag 01Y9, lemma-power-ideal-kills-sheaf; support comparison is Tag 07TY.

proof.text: For a fixed $n$, Step 1 identifies $(I^nF)|_U$ with $(J^nG)_{\mathrm{et}}$. The equivalence [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] detects zero, so this restriction vanishes exactly when $J^nG=0$. To see that restriction detects global zero without an unstated descent theorem, let $T\to X$ be any scheme object. By [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], the map $T\times_XU\to T$ is a surjective etale cover by a scheme. It is also an object over $U$. If a sheaf $H$ restricts to zero over $U$, each section in $H(T)$ restricts to zero on this cover and is zero by the separatedness part of the sheaf axiom [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus $H=0$; the converse is immediate. Apply this to $H=I^nF$ and combine with Step 4. This proves the equivalence in the item. No step uses reducedness of $Z$. If $X$ is empty or $F=0$, exponent zero works; if $Z$ is empty, the criterion says $F=0$; and if $Z=X$, exponent one works.
